text:
maria: quick heads-up — hit a weird onboarding snag in sample-kit v0.10.1. toolcall outputs that should be objects are coming in as escaped strings after an auth-refresh retry + streaming helper reconciliation.
jay: ouch. streaming + auth retry is a tricky combo. any short repro?
maria: yes — flow is: 1) SDK starts streaming tool result in json-mode (we emit chunks to preserve formatting) 2) auth token refresh triggers retry; retry layer re-sends the whole buffered payload but it was kept as rawText in the streamer 3) re-stringify wraps the rawText again, so downstream validate/schema helpers see '"{\"result\":1}"' instead of {"result":1}.
oliver: does this only happen when json-mode preserve setting is enabled?
maria: only when preserveStrings=true on the streaming helper AND the retry layer uses a naive JSON.stringify on whatever it has buffered. non-streaming, non-preserve paths unaffected.
sara: proposal: change the retry wrapper to normalize buffered payloads: if type === 'string' try JSON.parse, but only if it looks like JSON. also add a streaming buffer that tracks original object tokens instead of raw text.
jay: i'm wary of best-effort JSON.parse in retry code — could mask real text payloads. better: handshake contract between streamer and retry layer: streamer should expose getBufferedObject() OR getBufferedText(), explicit. then retry wrapper can choose raw vs structured resends.
maria: yep — that API would make parity easier too. right now node exposes bufferAsString() and py exposes buffer_tokens() which is inconsistent.
ci-bot: created issue #2701: "sdk: streaming json-mode + auth-retry can double-encode buffered tool payloads" assigned to @jay
oliver: test plan: add unit to streamer asserting bufferAsObject when preserveStrings=false; add integration that simulates token refresh mid-stream using auth-mock; assert consumer receives object typed payload after retry. include both node + python runners in the CI matrix.
sara: i'll draft the SDK helper spec: validateToolOutput(schema, { mode: 'strict'|'coerce'|'preserveStrings' }) and a StreamBuffer interface with explicit getters. share WIP in #devex tomorrow.
jay: temporary patch submitted to sample-kit that detects string-buffer and safe-parses before re-encoding: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-kit/pull/998. leaving a comment to revert once API is landed.
maria: thanks — workaround unblocks the customer onboarding. long-term, agree on explicit streamer<->retry contract and parity tests across runtimes.
ci-bot: pipeline: node-tests passed, py-tests failing on streaming-buffer spec — assigning to @oliver to investigate.
